en: The Banaue Rice Terraces act as a giant inclined plane, making it easier for farmers to carry crops up the mountain.
The Philippine tarsier has specialized toe pads that increase friction, allowing it to grip tree branches tightly while climbing.
Astronauts on the Apollo 11 moon landing experienced much less gravity than on Earth, allowing them to bounce while walking.
Japan’s SCMaglev train uses powerful magnets to levitate above the tracks, eliminating wheel friction to reach speeds over 600 km/h.
Alessandro Volta invented the voltaic pile, which was the world’s first electrical battery capable of producing a steady electric current.
The Cape Bojeador Lighthouse in Ilocos Norte uses large curved mirrors to reflect and focus light beams across the dark ocean.
Sperm whales produce extremely loud clicking sounds that travel for miles through the ocean to communicate and hunt prey.
The Tiwi Geothermal Power Plant in Albay generates electricity by harnessing the natural heat from hot rocks deep underground.
The Burgos Wind Farm in Ilocos Norte converts the kinetic energy of moving wind into electrical energy using giant turbines.
Water stored in the Magat Dam in Isabela possesses high gravitational potential energy before it flows down to spin turbines.
The sharp teeth of the Philippine crocodile act as wedges, a type of simple machine, to tear apart their food.
The copper wires connecting the San Roque Dam are excellent conductors because copper allows electric charges to flow easily.
